correctness.rationale: The source regularity criterion is verified in Theorem 2.3 of arXiv:2401.11741v1. Conditioning on center absent from domain gives rank-deficiency weights binom(m,j)(m+1)!/(j+1)! and ratio (m-j)/((j+1)(j+2)), whence J/sqrt(m) tends to one with exponentially small fixed-relative tails. Uniform conditional predecessor enumeration yields the exact L>=r product k/(m+1) times products (k-i)/(m+1-i), whose log tends to -x for r=floor(x sqrt(m)). An acyclic partial-injection Lah-number count gives conditional no-cycle probability (j+1)/(m+1), hence o(1). When cycles exist, the center lies in the image of f^t exactly for t<=L and a leaf does so for every t, proving T=L+1 by the source criterion. The independent exhaustive checker confirms all finite identities through n=6 and outputs VERIFY_OK. Finite cases alone would not establish the limit. The exact finite-size survival formula further counts all maps with the hub in the image of the t-th power using the conditional tail product, then subtracts maps whose t-th power has image exactly {hub}. Such exceptional maps have a hub-terminal chain of exactly t arrows and a forest of other ordered paths with at most t vertices; their count is m! times [z^(m-t)] exp(sum_{s=1}^t z^s). The independent checker verifies the resulting complete survival distribution through n=6.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new assertion is not the known regularity criterion or a count of monoid elements. Its substantive new quantifier is a limit over uniformly random full star-endomorphism monoids at the first regular power; reconstructing it requires combining prior structures with a conditional chain law and proving that acyclic exceptions are negligible. The prior general theory is the principal overlap risk. The explicit correction for cycle-free maps with t-th power of rank one is not the published static monoid cardinality or a direct table lookup. originality.rationale: The star-endomorphism source proves regularity of a single element, cardinalities and ranks, but not the first power becoming regular for a uniformly sampled element. The follow-up develops presentations. Ganyushkin-Mazorchuk provides relevant general partial-injection orbit and deficiency formulas and requires explicit acknowledgement: it does not state the star-specific first-regular-power exponential law in the inspected sections. The claim combines the source regularity obstruction, a new rank-conditioned terminal-chain survival product and a high-probability cycle argument to obtain the complete corrected finite-size survival formula and its nondegenerate limiting law. Search cannot prove priority; a general partial-injection hitting-time theorem remains a publication-priority risk. Janson-Mazorchuk (2005) already establishes sharp cardinality/defect distributions, and Laradji-Umar (2013) gives the bounded-path nilpotent generating function used in the finite correction; neither ingredient alone is claimed original.
residual_risks: A general partial-injection orbit-length asymptotic or power-regularity theorem could imply the result after specialization; complete publication priority is not established.
Search indexes and accessible full text do not cover every historical semigroup reference.
The bounded-path-forest correction is built from already-known nilpotent generating functions; only the combined first-regular-power distribution can be considered new.

value.rationale: The first positive power entering the regular part is a canonical dynamical semigroup statistic motivated directly by the exceptional nonregular elements identified by Dimitrova-Fernandes-Koppitz. Its order-sqrt(n) scale and nondegenerate Exp(1) fluctuations quantify a distinct phenomenon from known static regular-element counts and deterministic rank characterizations. The exact conditional predecessor-tail and cycle-free formula explain the stochastic mechanism and support possible comparison with other graph-endomorphism monoids. The all-dimensions exact formula determines every finite regularization-time multiplicity and isolates a nontrivial bounded-chain forest correction, strengthening the value beyond asymptotic order alone.
